other_side: Where this edition reads four models in a week as a market maturing beyond raw intelligence into interaction and fit, Zitron reads the same parade as the hype machine at full throttle. Every 'innovation', he argues, exists only because billions are burned to produce it, and the results remain more expensive and less useful than the people they claim to replace. Cheap models matching expensive ones is not differentiation to him but indictment: he notes Anthropic itself admitted that far cheaper models, including Kimi K2.7, found the same vulnerabilities as its flagship — proof the premium was never worth paying. And since hallucination is, per OpenAI's own research, "mathematically inevitable", no voice layer or orchestration pattern fixes the underlying trust problem. Nobody in the real world, he insists, cares about any of it.
truth_beneath: The variable both men orbit is whether model differentiation — interaction patterns, efficiency tiers, personality fit — represents real value creation or evidence the raw-capability race has stalled. Both accept two facts: cheap models now do most tasks roughly as well as frontier ones (Musk concedes it, Zitron celebrates it), and per-task costs for similar work vary as much as nine-fold. The empirical question that will resolve is whether the new tiers — full-duplex voice, cheap implementer models under frontier orchestrators — convert into durable paid usage; the observable that settles it is whether OpenAI and SpaceX AI revenue from these products grows over the next two quarters, or whether enterprise spend keeps being capped and consolidated downward. The residue is pure worldview: 'different, not just better' as product maturity versus plateau dressed as strategy. NLW is vindicated if interaction-layer products drive real new spending; Zitron if commoditisation crushes pricing while costs climb. Both are polemicists with incentives — NLW bullish and anti-doom, Zitron bubble-certain and anti-hype — and their accidental agreement is the signal: most work does not need frontier-priced intelligence. Watch GPT Live's paid adoption when numbers first surface.
